_purpose: What a model record must carry to be worth adding, and what each further step buys. Written 2026-11-20, because the catalogue had no entry criterion at all and so could grow without anyone being able to say whether it was improving.
_not_a_field_count: A level here is NOT how many fields are filled. It is which decision the engine can make because of them. Counting fields produces a number nobody can act on; naming the decision tells a contributor exactly what their five minutes would unlock. The levels also differ by HOW the facts are obtained, which is what makes them a plan rather than a label: one level the machine discovers by itself, the next a person has to read, the last an instrument has to measure.
_orthogonal_to_evidence: The level is completeness. It is NOT quality, and it never substitutes for the evidence rule: every field present, at every level, must have a source naming THAT device. A level-2 record with solid evidence is worth more than a level-3 record carrying a guessed chip family - the Gustard X30 was level 3 and simply wrong. A consumer's own documented/measured status answers a different question (how a fact was established) and the two compose: show both, conflate neither.
_why_partial_records_are_safe: An incomplete record can never make Auto worse than no record, because of how the cascade resolves: a field the record omits is inherited from the brand or the chip family, and a field nobody knows is "unknown", which makes the engine take the conservative branch. The danger is never missing data. It is data that is present and wrong, which is why the entry gate below is about evidence and identity rather than about filling boxes.

levels.name: Identified
levels.unlocks: The converter is recognised by name instead of being an unknown device, and resolves to its brand. Nothing else changes: it behaves exactly as the brand's catch-all.
levels.obtained_from: A USB descriptor, where the chain is USB: free, and exact. Otherwise a PERSON. What a network player announces of itself over UPnP names the RENDERER - the software serving the stream - and not the converter behind it, so turning an announcement into a device is a human act and is recorded as one.
levels._gate: A record at this level is admissible with EITHER an exact USB identity OR a resolved match (`device_match`) carrying its own evidence. With neither it resolves identically to the brand catch-all that already exists, so it is a duplicate row carrying no fact - and a row that looks like knowledge without being any is worse than an honest gap. With one of the two it earns its place, because it is what turns an unidentified device into a named one.
levels._relaxed_2026_11_24: The gate first asked for a USB identity and nothing else. That excluded every device the field can actually report: a player asks the network, and a UPnP announcement carries no USB descriptor at all. Worse, the announcement does not identify the hardware - it names the renderer software. One announced string routinely covers many different converters (upmpdcli, a Diretta bridge, or any player that announces itself all do this), and the brand announced is very often not the brand of the device. Both are verifiable by anyone on any UPnP network; the proportions were measured on a production export on 2026-11-24 and are recorded OUTSIDE this repository, with the editor's data. So the resolution is a claim like any other: it carries evidence, it can be contested, and it is NEVER inferred from the announced string alone.
levels._an_identity_can_be_generic: An identity does not always name a model, and a match must therefore say what it resolves TO. In this database `ta-dac200` carries one USB identity (0x1852/0x5034) across four products - DAC 200, HA 200, SDV 3100 HV, DAC8 DSD - and `mola-mola-generique` carries a VID/PID with `model: unknown`. A VID/PID can thus establish a range, or only a brand. That is why `device_match` names the subject it resolves to and the level it establishes, instead of assuming a device.

levels.name: Basic - what the device accepts
levels.unlocks: The whole PCM path, correctly: the rate ladder stops falling back to a conservative 192 kHz, the right ceiling applies per input, and DSD transport is known. This is the level the PCM-only Auto mode needs, and it needs nothing beyond it.
levels.obtained_from: THE PROBE GIVES THIS FOR FREE. Any player already asks a device what rates and formats it accepts; the contribution form carries the answer. Per-input ceilings are also the one thing makers reliably publish.
levels._this_is_the_target: Level 2 is where a record should normally enter, because it costs a contributor nothing and it is where the engine stops guessing.

levels.name: Advanced - what the device does inside
levels.unlocks: The DSD path: whether to send DSD at all, which modulator order, the level compensation so switching format does not change the volume, the real ladder depth to quantise to, and any rate at which the device steps its own processing aside.
levels.obtained_from: A datasheet, a maker's answer, or the reference implementation author's replies. NEVER a probe: no amount of asking a device what it accepts reveals what it does with it. This is the level that needs a person.
levels._the_hard_part: Makers publish the chip and the accepted formats. They do not publish the PCM/DSD level offset, whether DSD is re-converted internally, or a ladder's real depth as opposed to its interface's. Those four fields are why this level is slow, and browsing maker sites will not supply them.

levels.name: Measured
levels.unlocks: A per-device correction profile, and confirmation of the level-3 fields that were taken from documentation.
levels.obtained_from: Laboratory measurement of that device. This is the same thing a vendor catalogue means by "measured", so the two statuses are the same axis and should be one field, not two.
levels._state: No record in this catalogue is at this level, and none will be without hardware.

_state_2026_11_23: Measured across the 27 records on 2026-11-23 by replaying the engine over each one, with the cascade taken into account: 19 are complete at level 2 and 3 carry a USB identity, so the catalogue is essentially a level-2 catalogue. ZERO are complete at level 3, and the shortfall is concentrated exactly where documentation runs out - the real ladder depth is known for 7 records, an internal bypass for 1, the PCM/DSD offset for 16, and whether DSD is re-converted for 15. That distribution is the argument for the levels: the cheap half is nearly done and the expensive half has barely started, and a single completeness percentage would have hidden both facts. CORRECTED: the 2026-11-20 figure read 24 at level 2, because that count did not apply this file's own field list - it left out `inputs`, which 6 records do not carry. The four field counts were right. A self-description that does not run its own criterion is the one number nobody re-checks.
_state_2026_11_24: Measured on 2026-11-24 against this file's own field list, and re-measured after each change rather than carried over: 17 of the 25 records are complete at level 2, and 7 carry no input block. THE HISTORY OF THIS NUMBER, because it has been wrong twice and its denominator moved once: 24 of 27 until 2026-11-20 (a count that did not run this file's own criterion), 19 of 27, then 17 of 27, and 17 of 25 once two records left. Three rounds of withdrawal, each decided field by field against the record's own quoted source and never by analogy. First the per-input ceilings of chord/generique, ifi/generique and merging/hapi - one model's, asserted under a brand catch-all or a modular unit. Then the DEVICE-level ceilings of ifi/generique and msb/diamond, whose quotes carry no figure at all; MSB's entire evidence is the sentence « it is an R2R DAC (and thus native PCM) », which names no rate. Then two records left altogether - akm-generique and ess-generique - which called themselves « Fallback entry, not a measured device » and asserted, for a whole silicon line, the four fields _what_the_implementation_fixes says a chip does not fix. Their defaults live in chip-families, where they always belonged. TWO RECORDS WERE EXAMINED AND KEPT, which is why this says so: chord/generique's quote names both the rate and the brand (« passing 705.6/768k PCM to a Chord DAC »), so its pcm_max_hz is supported where iFi's and MSB's were not; and merging/hapi's figures are true of one Hapi, its defect being the SUBJECT - one record for every generation and fitted card - which is an identity question. Checking each field instead of removing for symmetry changed the answer twice: three withdrawals announced and two made, three records to delete and two deleted. THREE of the seven records with no input block still have no written reason that mentions inputs: mola-mola/generique, smsl/d6, unknown/unknown. The list was four, then five when a check that looked for the PRESENCE of a gloss was replaced by one that reads what it says, then three when two of the five were deleted. They are catch-alls, which is probably legitimate, and probably is not evidence.
